metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Omar, have you thought about getting a bottle of champagne for Adam's celebration? It could be a nice gift to toast his achievement. 

But... I’m not sure if it’s really fitting. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... I'm not really sure about champagne. In our culture, we often give more meaningful gifts, something personal that shows we care. Maybe a nice book or a framed photo of the group could be better? It would feel more special than just champagne. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
I get that, but I still think a bottle of champagne could be a fun way to celebrate. I mean, it’s a big deal, right? 

But I do wonder... do you strongly agree that making our parents proud is one of our main goals in life? I just feel like it shouldn't be our only focus.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand it's a big deal, but for me, making my parents proud is really important. It's about showing gratitude for all their hard work and sacrifices. I think that drives a lot of what we do. It’s not just about having fun, you know? I believe we can celebrate in a way that honors our families, too. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point, but I just don't think that should be the *main* goal for everyone. We should pursue our own dreams, not just what makes our parents proud. 

Back to Adam’s celebration... what about getting something that reflects his personality? Like, maybe a custom gift? It could still be meaningful without leaning on that pressure.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but for me, making my parents proud is still a priority. A custom gift could be nice, but it has to be something that really represents his achievement, too. Maybe a personalized trophy or something that celebrates his hard work? It can reflect his personality while also honoring the journey he took. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
A personalized trophy could work, I guess. It would definitely highlight his achievement. 

But I'm still really curious... you said making your parents proud drives a lot of what you do. What about your own happiness? Shouldn’t that matter just as much?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I don't know about that... it seems like making our parents proud and our own happiness can go hand in hand. At the end of the day, it's all the same, right? Different people have different priorities, and that's okay. As long as we're speaking the same language, I think we can all find a way to balance things. But about Adam’s gift, a personalized trophy sounds good, don’t you think? It really highlights his achievement.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message:
I guess a personalized trophy does highlight his achievement well. It could be a good compromise. 

But I still feel like we should prioritize our own paths, too. It’s just... I don’t want to feel like I’m always living for someone else’s expectations. 

Anyway, I think we can settle on the trophy. Want to help me find one?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand where you're coming from, but I still believe we can pursue our paths while also respecting our families. It's about finding that balance. But yes, let’s focus on the trophy for Adam. I can help you look for one. It’ll be great to celebrate what he’s accomplished together!
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious about something - it sounds like you both really care about honoring achievements, but might have different ways of showing that. Omar, I'm hearing how deeply important family recognition is for you, and Kelly, I sense you're emphasizing individual passion. Would you both be willing to share a bit about how your family backgrounds might shape how you think about success and celebration?

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message:
I think my family always encouraged me to follow my own path, and while they appreciate my achievements, they've never pressured me to live up to their expectations. That's why I feel it's important to celebrate our own successes, like Adam's, in a way that reflects who we are, not just what our parents want.

But I’m really curious, Omar, how has your family shaped your views on success and celebration?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: My family has always emphasized the importance of hard work and making sacrifices for a better future. They’ve shown me that success isn’t just about personal achievement; it’s about honoring those who supported us along the way. Celebrating achievements, like Adam's, is a way to show appreciation for my family's efforts. I feel that when we achieve something, we also represent our families and their dreams. That’s why making them proud is so significant to me.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message:
I totally agree! Adding some of our favorite memories would make it even more special. The scrapbook or video montage with those moments, plus the champagne, would create a really memorable celebration. 

I’m glad we found a way to combine both ideas. Adam is going to love it! Oh, and just one more thing—don’t you think focusing on our own individual dreams should come first, rather than making our parents proud? I feel like that’s what really matters in the long run.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I’m glad we’re on the same page about the gift! It’ll definitely make the celebration memorable for Adam. As for focusing on our individual dreams, I think that’s important too. But for me, making my parents proud will always be a big part of my journey. Their support and sacrifices inspire me to chase my dreams. I believe I can do both—follow my passions and honor my family's values. It’s a balance that works for me.
